messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Game day (simulated) incident created by @Miles Thornton
incident-bot: Channel: #incidents | Severity: SEV-3 (SIMULATION) | Doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Game+Day+-+Auto-rollback+SLO+Breach

Miles Thornton: starting game day now. Goal: validate auto-rollback wiring end-to-end (latency + error) + comms.
Miles Thornton: scenario 1 first: latency regression on canary. Route `chat.completions`, model `rw-openchat-7b`, rollout `rc-5121` (10% canary -> expect rollback to 0%).
Rafael Mendes: oncall role today. I’m watching paging + runbook flow. Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Auto-rollback+on+SLO+Breach
Benji Okafor: I’m on rollout-controller logs + traces. Rollout page: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/rc-5121
Leila Farouk: I’ll trigger the synthetic latency injector now.

deploy-bot: [staging] Applied config: `latency_inject_ms=450` for service `inference-gateway` route `chat.completions` (scope: canary only)

Sergio Costa: grafana panel already moving. p95 is climbing. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollout-slo/rollout-slo?var-rollout=rc-5121
Aisha Bello: what’s our policy for this route? p95 threshold 350ms over 5m window + min 200 req?
Allison Grant: yep. current proposed default for Hosted tier: p95 > 350ms for 5m, min_requests=200, warmup_grace=3m, cooldown=15m.
Miles Thornton: ok. clock started. expecting verdict “breach” and rollback within ~2-3 mins after window has enough data.

Benji Okafor: seeing evaluator tick. log line:
Benji Okafor: `slo_evaluator: monitor_fetch latency_p95 status=OK series=0 labels={route="chat.completions", model="rw-openchat-7b", region="us-east-1"}`
Benji Okafor: series=0 is… not great.
Nadia Rahman: series=0 means query returned empty. either we’re filtering out canary traffic label or monitor identity mismatch.
Sergio Costa: dashboard is showing latency though (so metrics exist). maybe the controller query uses `route_id` but dash uses `route_name`?
Allison Grant: can we paste the exact query template the controller is using?
Benji Okafor: from config (staging):
Benji Okafor: `p95(query="histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service='inference-gateway', route_id='${route}', model='${model}', region='${region}', tier='${tier}', rollout_id='${rollout_id}'}[${window}])) )")`
Nadia Rahman: there it is. gateway emits `route` not `route_id` in staging. prod has both but staging doesn’t. so the controller is basically blind.
Miles Thornton: so scenario 1 result: rollback will not trigger because it has “no data”. what does it do in that case? healthy? unknown?
Benji Okafor: right now it’s treating empty series as `healthy` (verdict=OK). that’s… yikes.
Sean Gallagher: for game day, that’s the key failure mode. no-data should be UNKNOWN at minimum. IMO should fail-open (don’t rollback) but must alert + surface loudly.
Rafael Mendes: +1. today this would silently not rollback and oncall wouldn’t know.
Hannah Rivera: also means incident-bot notifications wouldn’t fire (since no rollback event).
Allison Grant: action item: change semantics: empty series => UNKNOWN, emit `rollout.slo_verdict=unknown` metric + create alert/ticket.
Miles Thornton: ok, let’s keep going but call scenario 1 as “failed as expected due to labeling mismatch + bad unknown handling.”
Miles Thornton: Nadia can you confirm what label normalization PR in slo-toolkit is supposed to address? (route_id vs route)
Nadia Rahman: yep. slo-toolkit has a helper to map route_name->route_id. but rollout-controller isn’t using it yet.
Benji Okafor: also monitor identity contract doc says canonical is `route` not `route_id`. this is on us.

Leila Farouk: I can switch injector to emit `route_id` label quickly but that’s a hack. rather we fix the query.
Miles Thornton: agree. for scenario continuity, let’s patch the staging query template locally (just for game day) to use `route` label so we can verify rollback path.
Benji Okafor: I can hot-edit the template in staging config and restart rollout-controller.

deploy-bot: [staging] rollout-controller restarted (commit `b7f3c0a`) by @Benji Okafor
Benji Okafor: updated query to `route="${route}"` and removed rollout_id filter (we don’t have it consistently on latency hist yet).
Nadia Rahman: removing rollout_id means we’re now looking at overall route latency, not canary-specific. but ok for testing rollback mechanics.
Sean Gallagher: note that in real life that could cause correlated rollback across tenants if route latency is global. keep that in notes.

Sergio Costa: evaluator has data now. p95 620ms.
Benji Okafor: logs show `verdict=BREACH` after 2 eval ticks. waiting on executor.
Hannah Rivera: do we expect incident-bot message for the rollback trigger?
Benji Okafor: should emit audit event + Slack notification.

incident-bot: :warning: Auto-rollback trigger (SIMULATION)
incident-bot: Rollout: rc-5121 | Reason: latency_p95 breached threshold (p95=612ms > 350ms) | Action: revert traffic split to stable
incident-bot: Links: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/rc-5121 | Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Auto-rollback+on+SLO+Breach

Rafael Mendes: got the bot message. good.
Sergio Costa: traffic split looks like it moved? console says canary 0% now.
Benji Okafor: executor logs:
Benji Okafor: `rollback_executor: applied traffic_split stable=100 canary=0 idempotency_key=rc-5121:latency:1707760940`
Miles Thornton: ok. so scenario 1b (with patched query) rollback path works.
Miles Thornton: record outcome: default query template/labels wrong in staging; and empty-series semantics are currently unsafe.

Miles Thornton: scenario 2: error spike (5xx). We’ll flip injector for 5xx on canary only. Expect rollback + cooldown prevents immediate repeated triggers.
Leila Farouk: turning on 5xx injector (canary) now.

deploy-bot: [staging] Applied config: `error_inject_5xx_rate=0.25` for service `inference-gateway` route `chat.completions` (scope: canary only)

Aisha Bello: error monitor should be `5xx / total > 2%` over 3m, min 100 req. (that’s what’s in draft)
Allison Grant: yep.
Benji Okafor: evaluator sees error rate 18%.

incident-bot: :warning: Auto-rollback trigger (SIMULATION)
incident-bot: Rollout: rc-5121 | Reason: error_rate breached threshold (err=18.2% > 2.0%) | Action: revert traffic split to stable
incident-bot: Links: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/rc-5121 | Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Auto-rollback+on+SLO+Breach

Benji Okafor: executor attempted rollback again even though we’re already at canary=0.
Benji Okafor: log:
Benji Okafor: `rollback_executor: noop already_stable=true` (good) but it still emitted another audit event.
Rafael Mendes: that’s going to be noisy for oncall if both latency + error trip after the first rollback.
Sean Gallagher: we need dedupe: once rollback executed for a rollout, suppress further triggers for some TTL (or until new rollout state change).
Allison Grant: or set a “rolled_back_at” marker and evaluator stops evaluating unless rollout goes back into canary.
Hannah Rivera: +1 from notifications side; otherwise Slack spam.
Miles Thornton: ok, note that. Also check cooldown: did it respect 15m cooldown?
Benji Okafor: cooldown is keyed per monitor cause. so latency cause cooldown doesn’t suppress error cause. by design currently.
Sean Gallagher: design debate: cooldown should be per rollout, not per signal. at least for spam control.

Miles Thornton: scenario 3: monitoring outage / stale data. We’ll simulate monitor API returning 503 for a few minutes. Expect verdict UNKNOWN + no rollback, but alert/ticket.
Nadia Rahman: I can blackhole the monitor-proxy in staging.
Nadia Rahman: doing it for 3 mins.

deploy-bot: [staging] Applied network policy: `monitor-proxy egress=DENY` for namespace `rollout-controller`

Benji Okafor: monitor client errors now: `GET /api/v1/query timeout`.
Benji Okafor: verdict currently logs as `HEALTHY` (again). it falls back to last known good sample.
Allison Grant: that’s also unsafe. should be UNKNOWN if data is older than staleness threshold.
Aisha Bello: what’s the staleness cutoff?
Benji Okafor: none yet. it caches for 60s and reuses.
Sean Gallagher: we need explicit staleness window (e.g., if now - sample_ts > 2*scrape_interval + query_delay -> UNKNOWN). and that unknown should page? or ticket?
Rafael Mendes: for canary rollouts, I’d ticket unless customer impact. but at least surface in console.
Sergio Costa: also the dashboard would show “No data” / query errors, but controller hiding it is bad.
Hannah Rivera: and bot should send a different notification: “monitor fetch failed” not “rollback triggered.”
Miles Thornton: agreed. capture as breakage: monitoring dependency failure not handled.

Nadia Rahman: restoring monitor-proxy.

deploy-bot: [staging] Applied network policy: `monitor-proxy egress=ALLOW` for namespace `rollout-controller`

Benji Okafor: errors cleared.
Miles Thornton: ok. wrapping.
Miles Thornton: quick recap (please reply w/ anything I missed):
Miles Thornton: 1) Label mismatch (`route_id` vs `route`) caused empty series => rollback didn’t trigger. Worse: empty series treated as HEALTHY.
Miles Thornton: 2) With patched query, rollback executed correctly and bot notification worked.
Miles Thornton: 3) Error spike caused additional trigger; executor noop’d but still emitted event; cooldown is per-cause so spam risk.
Miles Thornton: 4) Monitor outage/staleness currently treated as “reuse cache => healthy”; needs UNKNOWN + surfaced + alerting.

Connor O'Brien: from release side: we should gate rollout of auto-rollback behind a feature flag until unknown semantics + label contract are fixed. also add a launch checklist item “monitor identity validated in target env.”
Leila Farouk: test harness note: our synthetic injector uses route_name; we should add an assertion that controller query returns non-empty series before the breach phase.
Allison Grant: I’ll open tickets for: unknown semantics + staleness threshold + align query template w/ monitor identity contract.
Rafael Mendes: I’ll update runbook: add step “check controller monitor fetch series_count + staleness” and add guidance for unknown verdict.
Sean Gallagher: + add an alert: `rollout_controller_monitor_fetch_errors` and `verdict_unknown_rate` (paging threshold TBD).
Hannah Rivera: I’ll adjust incident-bot formatting to include “verdict=UNKNOWN” case once we emit that event type.
Benji Okafor: I’ll take the implementation items. likely changes in evaluator + monitor client.
Miles Thornton: cool. please drop Linear links here once created. closing the sim incident in ~10.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Game day (simulated) incident resolved by @Miles Thornton (SEV-3 SIMULATION)
incident-bot: Post-game notes to be captured in doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Game+Day+-+Auto-rollback+SLO+Breach
